# Introduction
Growth references are an important tool for pediatricians to monitor growth in children. These growth references are often presented as percentile curves and exist for various anthropometric parameters (e.g., height, weight, body mass index (BMI)). To interpret a measurement from an individual child, pediatricians use tools to calculate a z-score or percentile of this measurement. A z-score,  also called standard deviation score, quantifies the difference between the mean ($\mu$) and the observation as a multiple of the standard deviation ($\sigma$). A z-score of 2 would translate to a distance of 2 standard deviations from the mean and to the `r trunc(pnorm(2)*100)`^th^ percentile.

## LMS Method
The WHO growth references were constructed with the Lambda-mu-sigma (LMS) method from [Cole et al.](https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.4780111005). Briefly, the distribution of a growth parameter (e.g., height, weight, BMI) in a specific age group is often a skewed normal distribution. The LMS method uses a box-cox power transformation of the growth parameter to obtain a normal distribution. Suppose y is a variable with a skewed normal distribution with median $\mu$, the transformed variable

$$
x = \frac{(y/\mu)^\lambda-1}{\lambda}
$${#eq-1}
will be normal distributed. The median $\mu$ of y gets mapped to x=0, and the coefficient of variation (CoV) of y corresponds approximately to the standard deviation $\sigma$ of x.
The z-score of x and of y can be calculated as

$$
z = \frac{x}{\sigma} = \frac{(y/\mu)^\lambda-1}{\lambda\sigma}
$${#eq-2}
, with $\sigma$ being the standard deviation of x.
The method gets its name from the $\lambda$-, $\mu$-, and $\sigma$-values, the LMS-values. L, M, and S are dependent on the age(t). L(t), S(t), and M(t) are fitted from the original distribution by a penalized likelihood method which results in smoothed natural cubic spline curves. The LMS-values are normally published in tables for various ages t.

## Need for interpolation

Publications of growth references include the LMS-values in the form of tables for certain ages (e.g., for every month from 0-18 years). The age of a child at the time of measurement can be determined more accurately (e.g., in days) by comparing the date of birth and the date of the measurement. Calculating z-scores based on LMS-values for a specific age in days is more accurate. Therefore, I interpolate the LMS-values for all ages (in days) that lie between the published LMS-values.

## Method for interpolation

In my code i normally use cubic interpolation, but i use linear interpolation at the borders. This is a similar method as the one used by the zanthro package for stata from [Vidmar et al.](https://doi.org/10.1177/1536867x1301300211)
As described above, the LMS method uses a penalized likelihood method which results in smoothed natural cubic spline curves. Hence, it makes sense to use cubic interpolation.

I use the following rules from the [Anthroplus Manual](https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/child-growth/growth-reference-5-19-years/who-anthroplus-manual.pdf) of the WHO to convert the age in years to months or days. I convert years to days by multiplying the number of years by 365.25. If the age is available in months I first divide the number of months by 12 and then multiply by 365.25 to get the age in days.

# Interpolation

I perform the interpolation for the following growth references.

- WHO ([WHO growth standards 0-5 years](https://www.doi.org/10.1111/j.1651-2227.2006.tb02378.x), [WHO growth references 5-19 years](https://www.doi.org/10.2471/blt.07.043497))
- [Braegger et al.](https://cdn.paediatrieschweiz.ch/production/uploads/2020/08/09-11.pdf)
- [Eiholzer et al.](https://www.doi.org/10.1080/03014460.2019.1677774)
- International Obesity Task Force, IOTF ([Cole and Lobstein](https://www.doi.org/10.1111/j.2047-6310.2012.00064.x))

## Load libraries and import data

The LMS-values were downloaded from the supplementary material of the mentioned publications. The data contains LMS values of height, weight, and BMI for various ages. The data from [Braegger et al.](https://cdn.paediatrieschweiz.ch/production/uploads/2020/08/09-11.pdf) is not open available on the internet. This data can be obtained from the secretariat of [paediatrieschweiz](https://www.paediatrieschweiz.ch/).
The WHO references can be downloaded on the WHO website: [WHO growth standards 0-5 years](https://www.who.int/tools/child-growth-standards), [WHO growth references 5-19 years](https://www.who.int/tools/growth-reference-data-for-5to19-years).

Import the libraries and the data into R.

```{r}
#| warning: false

```

## WHO references

The WHO child growth standards are already available in daily steps. They are published until the age of 5 years (day 1856). Therefore, I only need to interpolate the WHO growth references from the age 5 to 19 years. The WHO growth references are published in monthly steps from month 61 to month 228. Because day 1856 corresponds to an age just below month 61, I will use the WHO child growth standards until day 1856 and then use the WHO growth references from day 1857 onward. Day 1857 corresponds to an age just over month 61.

### Length

Body length (supine length) and body height (standing height) differ slightly when measured. In the Multi Growth Reference Study of the WHO the measured body length was on average 0.7 cm higher than the measured standing height. The length/height charts of the WHO child growth standards contain the supine length from 0-2 years, and the standing height from 2-5 years.
I therefore export the length references (0-2 years) separately from the height references (2-5 years + 5-19 years).

#### Boys
@fig-who-length-boys shows the published and interpolated LMS-values for height in boys. The curve of the M value corresponds to the 50^th^ percentile of length in boys in dependence of age.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false
#| label: fig-who-length-boys
#| fig-cap: "Published and interpolated LMS-values for length in boys based on the WHO child growth standards"
#| fig-height: 10


# filter length until/with day 730

who_length_boys <- who_height_boys_0_5 %>% 
  filter(Day <= 730) %>% 
  rename("age_days" = "Day")

# create plots
L_boys_plot <- ggplot(who_length_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=L))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("L (one)")+
  ggtitle("published LMS-values")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 3))

M_boys_plot <- ggplot(who_length_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=M))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("M (cm)")

S_boys_plot <- ggplot(who_length_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# create one figure with the 6 plots

interpolated_plot <- plot_grid(L_boys_plot, M_boys_plot, S_boys_plot, labels=c(), ncol=1)

# print the figure

interpolated_plot

# remove temporary variables
rm(L_boys_plot, M_boys_plot, S_boys_plot, interpolated_plot)

```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values
I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of length for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false


# add sex variable to LMS-values

who_length_boys <- who_length_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

who_length_girls <- who_length_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

who_length <- rbind(who_length_boys, who_length_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(who_length, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","who_length.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### Height

I will use the WHO child growth standards from 2-5 years and the WHO growth references from 5-19 years.
Calculate age in days and rename variables.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# calculate age in days in WHO growth references

who_height_boys_5_19 <- who_height_boys_5_19 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

who_height_girls_5_19 <- who_height_girls_5_19 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

# rename variable Day in WHO child growth standards

who_height_boys_0_5 <- who_height_boys_0_5 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Day) %>%
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

who_height_girls_0_5 <- who_height_girls_0_5 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Day) %>%
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

# merge two WHO datasets (WHO child growth standards 2-5 years and WHO growth references 5-19 years)

who_height_boys <- rbind(who_height_boys_0_5,who_height_boys_5_19) %>% 
  arrange(age_days) %>% 
  filter(age_days > 730)

who_height_girls <- rbind(who_height_girls_0_5,who_height_girls_5_19) %>% 
  arrange(age_days) %>% 
  filter(age_days > 730)

```

For the height parameter I do not need to interpolate the L-values, because they were always L = 0.
For the M- and S-values I do not need interpolation for the WHO child growth standards until month 60. I will use linear interpolation of the WHO growth references from month 61 to 62 (lower border), cubic interpolation from month 62 to 227, and linear interpolation from month 227 to 228 (upper border).

#### Boys

@fig-who-height-boys shows the published and interpolated LMS-values for height in boys. The curve of the M value corresponds to the 50^th^ percentile of height in boys in dependence of age.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false
#| label: fig-who-height-boys
#| fig-cap: "Published and interpolated LMS-values for height in boys based on the WHO references."
#| fig-height: 10

# L parameter was fixed at 1.

# plot of published L-values

L_boys_plot <- ggplot(who_height_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=L))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("L (one)")+
  ggtitle("published LMS-values")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 3))

# Therefore, no interpolation necessary, always L=1

xout <- seq(ceiling(2*365.25),ceiling(19*365.25), by=1)

new_L_boys <- data.frame(age_days = xout)
new_L_boys <- new_L_boys %>%
  mutate(L = 1)

# plot of interpolated L-values

L_boys_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_L_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=L))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("L (one)")+
  ggtitle("interpolated LMS-values")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 3))


# I need to interpolate the M parameter from the age 5 years (month 61, day 1857) onward.

# plot of published M-values

M_boys_plot <- ggplot(who_height_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=M))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("M (cm)")

# I will use linear interpolation from month 61 to 62, cubic from 62-227, and linear from 227-228.

# use WHO child growth standards from day 731 to day 1856.

new_M_1 <- who_height_boys_0_5 %>%
  select(age_days,M) %>% 
  filter(age_days >= 731)

# Interpolation from day 1857 to 6940

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(61/12*365.25),trunc(62/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- who_height_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(61/12*365.25)& age_days<=(62/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_M <- who_height_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(61/12*365.25)& age_days<=(62/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(M) %>% 
  unlist()
new_M_2 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_M,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_M_2 <- rename(new_M_2, "age_days" = "x", "M" = "y")

# cubic interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(62/12*365.25),trunc(227/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- who_height_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(62/12*365.25)& age_days<=(227/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_M <- who_height_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(62/12*365.25)& age_days<=(227/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(M) %>% 
  unlist()
new_M_3 <- data.frame(spline(x=x,y=y_M,xout=xout, method = "natural"))
new_M_3 <- rename(new_M_3, "age_days" = "x", "M" = "y")

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(227/12*365.25),ceiling(228/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- who_height_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(227/12*365.25) & age_days<=(228/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_M <- who_height_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(227/12*365.25) & age_days<=(228/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(M) %>% 
  unlist()
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of height for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_who_height_boys <- new_who_height_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_who_height_girls <- new_who_height_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_who_height <- rbind(new_who_height_boys, new_who_height_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_who_height, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_who_height.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```

### Weight

Calculate age in days and rename variables.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# calculate age in days

who_weight_boys_5_10 <- who_weight_boys_5_10 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

who_weight_girls_5_10 <- who_weight_girls_5_10 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

# rename variable Age in WHO child growth standards

who_weight_boys_0_5 <- who_weight_boys_0_5 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Day) %>%
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

who_weight_girls_0_5 <- who_weight_girls_0_5 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Day) %>%
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

# merge two WHO datasets (WHO child growth standards 0-5 years and WHO growth references 5-19 years)

who_weight_boys = rbind(who_weight_boys_0_5,who_weight_boys_5_10) %>% 
  arrange(age_days)

who_weight_girls = rbind(who_weight_girls_0_5,who_weight_girls_5_10) %>% 
  arrange(age_days)
```

I use linear interpolation from month 61 to 62 (lower border), cubic interpolation from month 62 to 119, and linear interpolation from month 119 to 120 (upper border).

```{r}
  theme_minimal()+

new_who_weight_boys <- merge(x=new_who_weight_boys, y=new_S_boys, by="age_days")

interpolated_plot <- plot_grid(L_boys_plot, L_boys_interpolated_plot, M_boys_plot, M_boys_interpolated_plot, S_boys_plot, S_boys_interpolated_plot, labels=c(), ncol=2)

interpolated_plot
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of weight for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_who_weight_boys <- new_who_weight_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_who_weight_girls <- new_who_weight_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_who_weight <- rbind(new_who_weight_boys, new_who_weight_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_who_weight, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_who_weight.csv"),  row.names=FALSE)
```

### BMI

Calculate age in days and rename variables.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# calculate age in days

who_bmi_boys_5_19 <- who_bmi_boys_5_19 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

who_bmi_girls_5_19 <- who_bmi_girls_5_19 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

# rename variable Age in WHO child growth standards

who_bmi_boys_0_5 <- who_bmi_boys_0_5 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Day) %>%
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

who_bmi_girls_0_5 <- who_bmi_girls_0_5 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Day) %>%
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

# merge two WHO datasets (WHO child growth standards 0-5 years and WHO growth references 5-19 years)

who_bmi_boys = rbind(who_bmi_boys_0_5,who_bmi_boys_5_19) %>% 
  arrange(age_days)

who_bmi_girls = rbind(who_bmi_girls_0_5,who_bmi_girls_5_19) %>% 
  arrange(age_days)
```

I use linear interpolation from month 61 to 62 (lower border), cubic interpolation from month 62 to 227, and linear interpolation from month 227 to 228 (upper border).

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of BMI for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_who_bmi_boys <- new_who_bmi_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_who_bmi_girls <- new_who_bmi_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_who_bmi <- rbind(new_who_bmi_boys, new_who_bmi_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_who_bmi, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_who_bmi.csv"),  row.names=FALSE)

interpolated_who_bmi <- interpolated_who_bmi %>% 
  mutate(sex = case_when(sex == "m" ~ 0,
                         sex == "f" ~ 1))

write.dta(interpolated_who_bmi, here(here("stata-scripts", "interpolated_who_bmi.dta")))
  
```

## Braegger references

The growth references of Braegger et al. are based on the WHO child growth standards and WHO growth references. The LMS-values of Braegger et al. are published in monthly steps, while the LMS-values of the WHO child growth standards are published in daily steps. To make use of the better accuracy of the WHO child growth standards, I use the LMS-values of the WHO child growth standards until month 61 (5 years). After the age of month 61, I will use the LMS-values published by Braegger et al. for interpolation.

### Length

Because Braegger et al. references are based on the WHO child growth standards I will use the length LMS values of the WHO child growth standards.

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# calculate age in days
braegger_length_boys <- braegger_height_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days, L,M,S)

braegger_length_girls <- braegger_height_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)%>% 
  select(age_days, L,M,S)

```

### Height

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# calculate age in days
braegger_height_boys <- braegger_height_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days, L,M,S) %>% 
  filter(age_days >730) %>% 
  slice(-1)

braegger_height_girls <- braegger_height_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)%>% 
  select(age_days, L,M,S) %>% 
  filter(age_days >730) %>% 
  slice(-1)

```

#### Boys

@fig-braegger-height-boys shows the published and interpolated LMS-values for height in boys. The curve of the M value corresponds to the 50^th^ percentile of height in boys in dependence of age.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false
#| label: fig-braegger-height-boys
#| fig-cap: "Published and interpolated LMS-values for height in boys based on the Braegger et al. references."
#| fig-height: 10

# L parameter was fixed at 1.

# plot of published L-values

L_boys_plot <- ggplot(braegger_height_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=L))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("L (one)")+
  ggtitle("published LMS-values")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 3))

# Therefore, no interpolation necessary, always L=1

xout <- seq(ceiling(2*365.25),ceiling(19*365.25), by=1)

new_L_boys <- data.frame(age_days = xout)
new_L_boys <- new_L_boys %>%
  mutate(L = 1)
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of height for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_braegger_height_boys <- new_braegger_height_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_braegger_height_girls <- new_braegger_height_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_braegger_height <- rbind(new_braegger_height_boys, new_braegger_height_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_braegger_height, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_braegger_height.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### Weight

The WHO child growth standards for weight cover the range from age 0 to 5 years. The WHO growth references for weight cover the range from age 5 to 10 years. Braegger et al. used data from the WHO Multicenter Growth Reference Study (0-5 years) and from the National Center for Health Statistics (5-18 years) to reconstruct the weight references until the age of 18 years.

As for the height, I will use the WHO child growth standards until the age of 5 years (month 61), because they are more accurate. After the age of 5 years (month 61) I will use the LMS-values published by Braegger et al. Because the LMS-values of Braegger et al. have a step/break at 8 years (original data from different studies), I will use linear interpolation around that break.

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false


# calculate age in days
braegger_weight_boys <- braegger_weight_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days, L,M,S)


braegger_weight_girls <- braegger_weight_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)%>% 
  select(age_days, L,M,S)
```

```{r}
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S = braegger_weight_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(62/12*365.25)& age_days<=(95/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_3 = data.frame(spline(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "natural"))
new_S_3 = rename(new_S_3, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# Because there is a break at 8 years (month 96 - 97), I will use linear interpolation around that break. I will carry the last value from month 96 forward until month 97.

# linear interpolation

xout = seq(ceiling(95/12*365.25),trunc(97/12*365.25),by=1)
x = braegger_weight_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(95/12*365.25) & age_days<=(96/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S = braegger_weight_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(95/12*365.25) & age_days<=(96/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_4 = data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear", rule = 2))
new_S_4 = rename(new_S_4, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# linear interpolation

xout = seq(ceiling(97/12*365.25),trunc(98/12*365.25),by=1)
x = braegger_weight_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(97/12*365.25)& age_days<=(98/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S = braegger_weight_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(97/12*365.25)& age_days<=(98/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_5 = data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_S_5 = rename(new_S_5, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# cubic interpolation

xout = seq(ceiling(98/12*365.25),trunc(215/12*365.25),by=1)
x = braegger_weight_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(98/12*365.25)& age_days<=(215/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S = braegger_weight_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(98/12*365.25)& age_days<=(215/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_6 = data.frame(spline(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "natural"))
new_S_6 = rename(new_S_6, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# linear interpolation

xout = seq(ceiling(215/12*365.25),ceiling(216/12*365.25),by=1)
x = braegger_weight_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(215/12*365.25)& age_days<=(216/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S = braegger_weight_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(215/12*365.25)& age_days<=(216/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_7 = data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_S_7 = rename(new_S_7, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# merge all S-values

new_S_girls = rbind(new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3, new_S_4, new_S_5, new_S_6, new_S_7)

# plot of interpolated S-values

S_girls_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_S_girls, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# merge all LMS-values

new_braegger_weight_girls = merge(x=new_L_girls, y=new_M_girls, by="age_days")
new_braegger_weight_girls = merge(x=new_braegger_weight_girls, y=new_S_girls, by="age_days")

# create one figure with the 6 plots

interpolated_plot <- plot_grid(L_girls_plot, L_girls_interpolated_plot, M_girls_plot, M_girls_interpolated_plot, S_girls_plot, S_girls_interpolated_plot, labels = c(), ncol=2)

# print the figure

interpolated_plot

# delete temporary variables

rm(L_girls_plot, L_girls_interpolated_plot, M_girls_plot, M_girls_interpolated_plot, S_girls_plot, S_girls_interpolated_plot, interpolated_plot, new_L_1, new_L_2, new_L_3, new_L_4, new_L_5, new_L_6, new_L_7, new_L_girls, new_M_1, new_M_2, new_M_3, new_M_4, new_M_5, new_M_6, new_M_7, new_M_8, new_M_girls, new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3, new_S_4, new_S_5, new_S_6, new_S_7, new_S_girls)
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of height for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_braegger_weight_boys <- new_braegger_weight_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_braegger_weight_girls <- new_braegger_weight_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_braegger_weight <- rbind(new_braegger_weight_boys, new_braegger_weight_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_braegger_weight, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_braegger_weight.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```

### BMI

For the BMI there are no special conditions and I use the same criteria for interpolation as for the height.

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# calculate age in days
braegger_bmi_boys <- braegger_bmi_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days, L,M,S)

braegger_bmi_girls <- braegger_bmi_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)%>% 
  select(age_days, L,M,S)

```

```{r}
# I will use linear interpolation from month 61 to 62, cubic from 62-227, and linear from 227-228.

# use WHO child growth standards from day 0 to day 1856.

new_S_1 <- who_bmi_girls_0_5 %>% 
  select(age_days,S)

# Interpolation from day 1857 to 6940

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(61/12*365.25),trunc(62/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- braegger_bmi_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(61/12*365.25)& age_days<=(62/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- braegger_bmi_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(61/12*365.25)& age_days<=(62/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_2 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_S_2 <- rename(new_S_2, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# cubic interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(62/12*365.25),trunc(227/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- braegger_bmi_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(62/12*365.25)& age_days<=(227/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- braegger_bmi_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(62/12*365.25)& age_days<=(227/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_3 <- data.frame(spline(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "natural"))
new_S_3 <- rename(new_S_3, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(227/12*365.25),ceiling(228/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- braegger_bmi_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(227/12*365.25) & age_days<=(228/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- braegger_bmi_girls %>%
  filter(age_days>=(227/12*365.25) & age_days<=(228/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_4 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear", rule = 2))
new_S_4 <- rename(new_S_4, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# merge all S-values

new_S_girls <- rbind(new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3, new_S_4)

# plot of interpolated S-values

S_girls_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_S_girls, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# merge all LMS-values

new_braegger_bmi_girls <- merge(x=new_L_girls, y=new_M_girls, by="age_days")
new_braegger_bmi_girls <- merge(x=new_braegger_bmi_girls, y=new_S_girls, by="age_days")

# create one figure with the 6 plots

interpolated_plot <- plot_grid(L_girls_plot, L_girls_interpolated_plot, M_girls_plot, M_girls_interpolated_plot, S_girls_plot, S_girls_interpolated_plot, labels = c(), ncol=2)

# print the figure

interpolated_plot


# delete temporary variables
rm(L_girls_plot, L_girls_interpolated_plot, M_girls_plot, M_girls_interpolated_plot, S_girls_plot, S_girls_interpolated_plot, interpolated_plot, new_L_1, new_L_2, new_L_3, new_L_4, new_L_girls, new_M_1, new_M_2, new_M_3, new_M_4, new_M_girls, new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3, new_S_4, new_S_girls)
```


#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of BMI for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_braegger_bmi_boys <- new_braegger_bmi_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_braegger_bmi_girls <- new_braegger_bmi_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_braegger_bmi <- rbind(new_braegger_bmi_boys, new_braegger_bmi_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_braegger_bmi, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_braegger_bmi.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### Head circumference

The head circumference references from Braegger et al. are from the Zurich Longitudinal studies, similar to the ones from [Prader et al.](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/2737921).

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# calculate age in days
braegger_hc_boys <- braegger_hc_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

braegger_hc_girls = braegger_hc_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

```

#### Boys

```{r}
#| output: true
```

```{r}
# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_braegger_hc_boys <- new_braegger_hc_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_braegger_hc_girls <- new_braegger_hc_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")
```

### Height velocity

The height velocity references from Braegger et al. are the ones from [Prader et al.](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/2737921)
The velocity references include means and standard deviations. Because the data was nearly normal distributed, we can set the L parameter at L=1.

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false


# calculate age in days
braegger_height_velocity_boys <- braegger_height_velocity_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Alter*365.25) %>% 
  rename("M" = "Mittelwert") %>% 
  mutate(S = SD/M,
         L= 1) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

braegger_height_velocity_girls = braegger_height_velocity_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Alter*365.25) %>% 
  rename("M" = "Mittelwert") %>% 
  mutate(S = SD/M,
         L = 1) %>% 
  select(age_days,L,M,S)

```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the M- and SD-values of height velocity for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_braegger_height_velocity_boys <- new_braegger_height_velocity_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_braegger_height_velocity_girls <- new_braegger_height_velocity_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_braegger_height_velocity <- rbind(new_braegger_height_velocity_boys, new_braegger_height_velocity_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_braegger_height_velocity, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_braegger_height_velocity.csv"), row.names=FALSE)

```



## PEZZ references 2019

The growth references of the PEZZ (Eiholzer et al., 2019) are based on a cross-sectional study performed in Switzerland in the regions of Zurich and Central Switzerland. The LMS-values for boys are published until the age of 20 years; the LMS-values for girls are published until the age of 18 years.

### Length/Height

Eiholzer et al. reported that body height was measured in supine position as length for children younger than 2 years. Unfortunately, they do not report how they addressed the change of length to height at the age of 2 years. From their publication it seems that they used one model to smoothen the whole period from 0 to 20 years. I therefore interpolate and export the length/height references as one from 0-20 years.

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false


# calculate age in days
eiholzer_height_boys_19 = eiholzer_height_boys_19 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

eiholzer_height_girls_19 = eiholzer_height_girls_19 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of height for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_eiholzer_height_boys_19 <- new_eiholzer_height_boys_19 %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_eiholzer_height_girls_19 <- new_eiholzer_height_girls_19 %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_eiholzer_height_19 <- rbind(new_eiholzer_height_boys_19, new_eiholzer_height_girls_19)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_eiholzer_height_19, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_eiholzer_height_19.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of weight for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_eiholzer_weight_boys_19 <- new_eiholzer_weight_boys_19 %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_eiholzer_weight_girls_19 <- new_eiholzer_weight_girls_19 %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_eiholzer_weight_19 <- rbind(new_eiholzer_weight_boys_19, new_eiholzer_weight_girls_19)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_eiholzer_weight_19, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_eiholzer_weight_19.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### BMI

The LMS-values for BMI are published from 2 years to 20 years for boys and from 2 years to 18 years for girls.

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# calculate age in days
eiholzer_bmi_boys_19 = eiholzer_bmi_boys_19 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)


eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 = eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)
```

```{r}
S_girls_plot <- ggplot(eiholzer_bmi_girls_19, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# I will use linear interpolation from year 0 to 0.08, cubic from 0.08 to 17.5, and linear from 17.5 to 18.

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(trunc(2*365.25),trunc(2.5*365.25),by=1)
x <- eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 %>%
  filter(age_days>=(2*365.25)& age_days<=(2.5*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 %>%
  filter(age_days>=(2*365.25)& age_days<=(2.5*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_1 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_S_1 <- rename(new_S_1, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# cubic interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(2.5*365.25),trunc(17.5*365.25),by=1)
x <- eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 %>%
  filter(age_days>=(2.5*365.25)& age_days<=(17.5*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 %>%
  filter(age_days>=(2.5*365.25)& age_days<=(17.5*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_2 <- data.frame(spline(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "natural"))
new_S_2 <- rename(new_S_2, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(17.5*365.25),ceiling(18*365.25),by=1)
x <- eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 %>%
  filter(age_days>=(17.5*365.25) & age_days<=(18*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 %>%
  filter(age_days>=(17.5*365.25) & age_days<=(18*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_3 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear", rule = 2))
new_S_3 <- rename(new_S_3, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# merge all S-values

new_S_girls <- rbind(new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3)

# plot of interpolated S-values

S_girls_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_S_girls, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# merge all LMS-values

new_eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 <- merge(x=new_L_girls, y=new_M_girls, by="age_days")
new_eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 <- merge(x=new_eiholzer_bmi_girls_19, y=new_S_girls, by="age_days")

# create one figure with the 6 plots

interpolated_plot <- plot_grid(L_girls_plot, L_girls_interpolated_plot, M_girls_plot, M_girls_interpolated_plot, S_girls_plot, S_girls_interpolated_plot, labels = c(), ncol=2)

# print the figure

interpolated_plot

# delete temporary variables

rm(L_girls_plot, L_girls_interpolated_plot, M_girls_plot, M_girls_interpolated_plot, S_girls_plot, S_girls_interpolated_plot, interpolated_plot, new_L_1, new_L_2, new_L_3, new_L_girls, new_M_1, new_M_2, new_M_3, new_M_girls, new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3, new_S_girls)
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of BMI for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_eiholzer_bmi_boys_19 <- new_eiholzer_bmi_boys_19 %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 <- new_eiholzer_bmi_girls_19 %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_eiholzer_bmi_19 <- rbind(new_eiholzer_bmi_boys_19, new_eiholzer_bmi_girls_19)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_eiholzer_bmi_19, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_eiholzer_bmi_19.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```



## PEZZ references 2025

The growth references of the PEZZ (Eiholzer et al., 2025) were updated with data collection in Ticino and Romandie. The LMS-values for boys are published until the age of 20 years; the LMS-values for girls are published until the age of 18 years.

### Length/Height

Eiholzer et al. reported that body height was measured in supine position as length for children younger than 2 years. Unfortunately, they do not report how they addressed the change of length to height at the age of 2 years. From their publication it seems that they used one model to smoothen the whole period from 0 to 20 years. I therefore interpolate and export the length/height references as one from 0-20 years.

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false


# calculate age in days
eiholzer_height_boys_25 = eiholzer_height_boys_25 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

eiholzer_height_girls_25 = eiholzer_height_girls_25 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

```

#### Boys

@fig-eiholzer-height-boys shows the published and interpolated LMS-values for height in boys. The curve of the M value corresponds to the 50^th^ percentile of height in boys in dependence of age.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false
#| label: fig-eiholzer-height-boys
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of weight for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_eiholzer_weight_boys_25 <- new_eiholzer_weight_boys_25 %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_eiholzer_weight_girls_25 <- new_eiholzer_weight_girls_25 %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_eiholzer_weight_25 <- rbind(new_eiholzer_weight_boys_25, new_eiholzer_weight_girls_25)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_eiholzer_weight_25, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_eiholzer_weight_25.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### BMI

The LMS-values for BMI are published from 2 years to 20 years for boys and from 2 years to 18 years for girls.

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# calculate age in days
eiholzer_bmi_boys_25 = eiholzer_bmi_boys_25 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)


eiholzer_bmi_girls_25 = eiholzer_bmi_girls_25 %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of BMI for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_eiholzer_bmi_boys_25 <- new_eiholzer_bmi_boys_25 %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_eiholzer_bmi_girls_25 <- new_eiholzer_bmi_girls_25 %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_eiholzer_bmi_25 <- rbind(new_eiholzer_bmi_boys_25, new_eiholzer_bmi_girls_25)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_eiholzer_bmi_25, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_eiholzer_bmi_25.csv"), row.names=FALSE)

```



## IOTF references

The LMS-values of the IOTF references for BMI are published from 2 years to 18 years for boys and girls.

### BMI

Calculate age in days.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false


# calculate age in days
iotf_bmi_boys = iotf_bmi_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)


iotf_bmi_girls = iotf_bmi_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of height for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_iotf_bmi_boys <- new_iotf_bmi_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_iotf_bmi_girls <- new_iotf_bmi_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_iotf_bmi <- rbind(new_iotf_bmi_boys, new_iotf_bmi_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_iotf_bmi, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_iotf_bmi.csv"), row.names=FALSE)

# export the data frame as a stata file


interpolated_iotf_bmi <- interpolated_iotf_bmi %>% 
  mutate(sex = case_when(sex == "m" ~ 0,
                         sex == "f" ~ 1))

write.dta(interpolated_iotf_bmi, here(here("stata-scripts", "interpolated_iotf_bmi.dta")))

```

## Prader references

The growth references of Prader et al. were not created with the LMS method. They reported means, standard deviations, and empirical percentiles for normal distributed data and just empirical percentiles for non normal distributed data.
I will use heuristic L and S values from Hermanussen et al. to convert the Prader references into the LMS format.

### Length

The length is reported from 0 to 15 years and was normal distributed. Therefore, I will use L = 1 and S estimated from the centiles.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add L values
# The L value is fixed to 1 because they reported a good accordance with a normal distribution

prader_length_boys <- prader_length_boys %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)

prader_length_girls <- prader_length_girls %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)


# calculate S values
prader_length_boys <- prader_length_boys %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_10/M)/(qnorm(0.10)),
                                           log(emp_perc_25/M)/(qnorm(0.25)),
                                           log(emp_perc_75/M)/(qnorm(0.75)),
                                           log(emp_perc_90/M)/(qnorm(0.90)),
                                           log(emp_perc_97/M)/(qnorm(0.97)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_length_boys <- prader_length_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)


prader_length_girls <- prader_length_girls %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_length_girls <- prader_length_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)

# calculate age in days
prader_length_boys <- prader_length_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

prader_length_girls <- prader_length_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

```

#### Check centiles

```{r}

new_prader_length_boys <- new_prader_length_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_length_girls <- new_prader_length_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")



interpolated_prader_length <- rbind(new_prader_length_boys, new_prader_length_girls)

interpolated_prader_length <- interpolated_prader_length |> 
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25)


z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)

interpolated_prader_length <- interpolated_prader_length |> 
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))


prader_length_boys <- prader_length_boys |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)

prader_length_girls <- prader_length_girls |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)


interpolated_prader_length |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_50, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_75, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_90, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_97, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_3, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_10, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_25, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_50, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_75, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_90, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_97, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  scale_y_continuous(name = "length [cm]",
                     limits = c(45, 200), breaks= c(50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 175, 200), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Age [years]",
                     limits = c(0, 20), breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 20), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("LMS centiles" = "blue", "Empirical centiles" = "black"))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 0.5, l = 0.5, b = 0, unit = "cm"))



interpolated_prader_length |>
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of length for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_prader_length_boys <- new_prader_length_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_length_girls <- new_prader_length_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_prader_length <- rbind(new_prader_length_boys, new_prader_length_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_prader_length, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_prader_length.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### Height

The height was reported from 3 to 20 years and was normally distributed. I will use L = 1 and estimate S from the centiles.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add L values
# The L value is fixed to 1 because they reported a good accordance with a normal distribution

prader_height_boys <- prader_height_boys %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)

prader_height_girls <- prader_height_girls %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)


# calculate S values
prader_height_boys <- prader_height_boys %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_10/M)/(qnorm(0.10)),
                                           log(emp_perc_25/M)/(qnorm(0.25)),
                                           log(emp_perc_75/M)/(qnorm(0.75)),
                                           log(emp_perc_90/M)/(qnorm(0.90)),
                                           log(emp_perc_97/M)/(qnorm(0.97)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_height_boys <- prader_height_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)


prader_height_girls <- prader_height_girls %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_height_girls <- prader_height_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)

# calculate age in days
prader_height_boys <- prader_height_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

prader_height_girls <- prader_height_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

```

```{r}
  filter(age_days>=(3*365.25)& age_days<=(4*365.25)) %>%

  unlist()
y_S <- prader_height_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(3*365.25)& age_days<=(4*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_1 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_S_1 <- rename(new_S_1, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# cubic interpolation

  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()

new_S_2 <- rename(new_S_2, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

  filter(age_days>=(19*365.25) & age_days<=(20*365.25)) %>%

  unlist()

  filter(age_days>=(19*365.25) & age_days<=(20*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()

new_S_3 <- rename(new_S_3, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# merge all M-values

new_S_boys <- rbind(new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3)

# plot of interpolated S-values

S_boys_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_S_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# merge all LMS-values

new_prader_height_boys <- merge(x=new_L_boys, y=new_M_boys, by="age_days")
new_prader_height_boys <- merge(x=new_prader_height_boys, y=new_S_boys, by="age_days")

# create one figure with the 6 plots

interpolated_plot
```

#### Check centiles

```{r}

new_prader_height_boys <- new_prader_height_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_height_girls <- new_prader_height_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")



interpolated_prader_height <- rbind(new_prader_height_boys, new_prader_height_girls)

interpolated_prader_height <- interpolated_prader_height |> 
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25)


z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)

interpolated_prader_height <- interpolated_prader_height |> 
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))


prader_height_boys <- prader_height_boys |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)

prader_height_girls <- prader_height_girls |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)


interpolated_prader_height |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_50, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_75, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_90, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_97, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_point(data = prader_height_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_3, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_height_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_10, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_height_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_25, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_height_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_50, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_height_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_75, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_height_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_90, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_height_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_97, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  scale_y_continuous(name = "height [cm]",
                     limits = c(45, 200), breaks= c(50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 175, 200), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Age [years]",
                     limits = c(0, 20), breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 20), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("LMS centiles" = "blue", "Empirical centiles" = "black"))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 0.5, l = 0.5, b = 0, unit = "cm"))



interpolated_prader_height |>
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of height for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_prader_height_boys <- new_prader_height_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_height_girls <- new_prader_height_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_prader_height <- rbind(new_prader_height_boys, new_prader_height_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_prader_height, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_prader_height.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### Weight

The weight was reported from 0 to 20 years.
They reported normally distributed weights until 10 years for boys and until 9 years for girls. I will still use heuristic L values from Hermanussen et al. and estimate the S values from the empirical centiles.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false


# add heuristic L values
prader_weight_boys <- left_join(prader_weight_boys, hermanussen_weight_boys, by = "Age")

prader_weight_girls <- left_join(prader_weight_girls, hermanussen_weight_girls, by = "Age")

# optimize L values

prader_weight_boys <- prader_weight_boys |> 
  mutate(L = case_when(Age == 0.08 ~ 0.8,
                       Age == 0.25 ~ 0.7,
                       Age == 0.75 ~ 0.5,
                       Age == 10.5 ~ -0.8,
                       Age == 11.5 ~ -0.7,
                       Age == 12.5 ~ -0.6,
                       Age == 13.5 ~ -0.3,
                       Age == 14 ~ -0.2,
                       Age == 14.5 ~ 0,
                       Age == 15 ~ 0,
                       Age == 15.5 ~ -0.1,
                       Age == 16 ~ -0.2,
                       Age == 17 ~ -0.6,
                       Age == 18 ~ -1.2,
                       Age == 19 ~ -1,
                       Age == 20 ~ -0.6,
                       TRUE ~ L))


prader_weight_girls <- prader_weight_girls |> 
  mutate(L = case_when(Age == 0.08 ~ 1,
                       Age == 0.25 ~ 0.8,
                       Age == 0.75 ~ 0.4,
                       Age == 4 ~ -0.2,
                       Age == 5 ~ -0.2,
                       Age == 6 ~ -0.2,
                       Age == 7 ~ -0.2,
                       Age == 8 ~ -0.2,
                       Age == 9 ~ -0.4,
                       Age == 9.5 ~ -0.5,
                       Age == 10.5 ~ -0.6,
                       Age == 11 ~ -0.6,
                       Age == 11.5 ~ -0.5,
                       Age == 12 ~ -0.4,
                       Age == 12.5 ~ -0.3,
                       Age == 13 ~ -0.2,
                       Age == 13.5 ~ -0.1,
                       Age == 14 ~ -0.1,
                       Age == 14.5 ~ -0.2,
                       Age == 15 ~ -0.6,
                       Age == 15.5 ~ -1.0,
                       Age == 16 ~ -1.4,
                       Age == 17 ~ -1.8,
                       Age == 18 ~ -2,
                       Age == 19 ~ -1.6,
                       Age == 20 ~ -1.2,
                       TRUE ~ L))
  

# calculate age in days
prader_weight_boys <- prader_weight_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

prader_weight_girls <- prader_weight_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

# calculate S values
prader_weight_boys <- prader_weight_boys %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_10/M)/(qnorm(0.10)),
                                           log(emp_perc_25/M)/(qnorm(0.25)),
                                           log(emp_perc_75/M)/(qnorm(0.75)),
                                           log(emp_perc_90/M)/(qnorm(0.90)),
                                           log(emp_perc_97/M)/(qnorm(0.97)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_weight_boys <- prader_weight_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)


prader_weight_girls <- prader_weight_girls %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_weight_girls <- prader_weight_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)

```

```{r}
# cubic interpolation

x <- prader_weight_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(0.08*365.25)& age_days<=(19*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
```

#### Check centiles

```{r}

new_prader_weight_boys <- new_prader_weight_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_weight_girls <- new_prader_weight_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")



interpolated_prader_weight <- rbind(new_prader_weight_boys, new_prader_weight_girls)

interpolated_prader_weight <- interpolated_prader_weight |> 
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25)


z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)

interpolated_prader_weight <- interpolated_prader_weight |> 
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))


prader_weight_boys <- prader_weight_boys |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)

prader_weight_girls <- prader_weight_girls |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)


interpolated_prader_weight |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_50, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_75, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_90, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_97, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_point(data = prader_weight_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_3, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_weight_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_10, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_weight_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_25, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_weight_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_50, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_weight_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_75, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_weight_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_90, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_weight_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_97, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Weight [cm]",
                     limits = c(0, 100), breaks= c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Age [years]",
                     limits = c(0, 20), breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 20), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("LMS centiles" = "blue", "Empirical centiles" = "black"))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 0.5, l = 0.5, b = 0, unit = "cm"))



interpolated_prader_weight |> 
  filter(sex == "f") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of weight for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_prader_weight_boys <- new_prader_weight_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_weight_girls <- new_prader_weight_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_prader_weight <- rbind(new_prader_weight_boys, new_prader_weight_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_prader_weight, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_prader_weight.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```



### BMI

Prader et al. did not publish any BMI values.
I therefore calculate a median BMI value from the median weight and height values.
I add heuristic L and S values for BMI from Hermanussen et al.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# correct M values
# The M values of height below 3 years of age were measured as supine length (lying). I therefore substract 0.7 cm from every M value if the Age is below 3 years.

prader_length_boys_bmi <- prader_length_boys %>% 
  filter(Age < 3) %>% 
  mutate(M = M-0.7) %>%
  select(Age, M)

prader_length_girls_bmi <- prader_length_girls %>% 
  filter(Age < 3) %>% 
  mutate(M = M-0.7) %>%
  select(Age, M)

# Create M values for BMI
prader_height_boys_bmi <- prader_height_boys %>% 
  select(Age, M) %>% 
  bind_rows(prader_length_boys_bmi)

prader_height_girls_bmi <- prader_height_girls %>% 
  select(Age, M) %>% 
  bind_rows(prader_length_girls_bmi)


prader_weight_boys_bmi <- prader_weight_boys %>% 
  select(Age, M)

prader_weight_girls_bmi <- prader_weight_girls %>% 
  select(Age, M)

prader_bmi_boys <- left_join(prader_height_boys_bmi, prader_weight_boys_bmi, by = "Age") %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  rename("M_height"= "M.x",
         "M_weight"= "M.y")

prader_bmi_boys <- prader_bmi_boys %>% 
  mutate(M = M_weight/(M_height/100)^2)



prader_bmi_girls <- left_join(prader_height_girls_bmi, prader_weight_girls_bmi, by = "Age") %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  rename("M_height"= "M.x",
         "M_weight"= "M.y")

prader_bmi_girls <- prader_bmi_girls %>% 
  mutate(M = M_weight/(M_height/100)^2)

# add L and S values

prader_bmi_boys <- left_join(prader_bmi_boys, hermanussen_bmi_boys, by = "Age")

prader_bmi_girls <- left_join(prader_bmi_girls, hermanussen_bmi_girls, by = "Age")

# filter Age until 18 years, because heuristic LS values only go from 0 to 18 years.

prader_bmi_boys <- prader_bmi_boys %>% 
  filter(Age <= 18)

prader_bmi_girls <- prader_bmi_girls %>% 
  filter(Age <= 18)

# calculate age in days
prader_bmi_boys <- prader_bmi_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

prader_bmi_girls <- prader_bmi_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

```

### Head circumference

The head circumference is reported from 0.08 to 19 years and was normal distributed. Therefore, I will use L = 1 and S = SD/M.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add L values
# The L value is fixed to 1 because they reported a good accordance with a normal distribution

prader_hc_boys <- prader_hc_boys %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)

prader_hc_girls <- prader_hc_girls %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)


# calculate S values
prader_hc_boys <- prader_hc_boys %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_10/M)/(qnorm(0.10)),
                                           log(emp_perc_25/M)/(qnorm(0.25)),
                                           log(emp_perc_75/M)/(qnorm(0.75)),
                                           log(emp_perc_90/M)/(qnorm(0.90)),
                                           log(emp_perc_97/M)/(qnorm(0.97)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_hc_boys <- prader_hc_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)


prader_hc_girls <- prader_hc_girls %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_hc_girls <- prader_hc_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)

# calculate age in days
prader_hc_boys <- prader_hc_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

prader_hc_girls <- prader_hc_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

```

#### Check centiles

```{r}

new_prader_hc_boys <- new_prader_hc_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_hc_girls <- new_prader_hc_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")



interpolated_prader_hc <- rbind(new_prader_hc_boys, new_prader_hc_girls)

interpolated_prader_hc <- interpolated_prader_hc |> 
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25)


z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)

interpolated_prader_hc <- interpolated_prader_hc |> 
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))


prader_hc_boys <- prader_hc_boys |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)

prader_hc_girls <- prader_hc_girls |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)


interpolated_prader_hc |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_50, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_75, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_90, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_97, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_point(data = prader_hc_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_3, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_hc_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_10, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_hc_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_25, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_hc_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_50, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_hc_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_75, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_hc_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_90, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_hc_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_97, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  scale_y_continuous(name = "hc [cm]", expand = c(0,0))+

  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),

        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 0.5, l = 0.5, b = 0, unit = "cm"))
```
