#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of head circumference for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_prader_hc_boys <- new_prader_hc_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_hc_girls <- new_prader_hc_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_prader_head_circumference <- rbind(new_prader_hc_boys, new_prader_hc_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_prader_head_circumference, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_prader_head_circumference.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### Height velocity

The velocity for standing height is reported from 2.5 to 19.5 years and was normal distributed. Therefore, I will use L = 1 and S = SD/M.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add L values
# The L value is fixed to 1 because they reported a good accordance with a normal distribution

prader_velocity_boys <- prader_velocity_boys %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)

prader_velocity_girls <- prader_velocity_girls %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)


# calculate S values
prader_velocity_boys <- prader_velocity_boys %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_10/M)/(qnorm(0.10)),
                                           log(emp_perc_25/M)/(qnorm(0.25)),
                                           log(emp_perc_75/M)/(qnorm(0.75)),
                                           log(emp_perc_90/M)/(qnorm(0.90)),
                                           log(emp_perc_97/M)/(qnorm(0.97)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_velocity_boys <- prader_velocity_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)


prader_velocity_girls <- prader_velocity_girls %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_velocity_girls <- prader_velocity_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)

# calculate age in days
prader_velocity_boys <- prader_velocity_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

prader_velocity_girls <- prader_velocity_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)


```

#### Check centiles

```{r}

new_prader_velocity_boys <- new_prader_velocity_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_velocity_girls <- new_prader_velocity_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")



interpolated_prader_velocity <- rbind(new_prader_velocity_boys, new_prader_velocity_girls)

interpolated_prader_velocity <- interpolated_prader_velocity |> 
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25)


z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)

interpolated_prader_velocity <- interpolated_prader_velocity |> 
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))


prader_velocity_boys <- prader_velocity_boys |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)

prader_velocity_girls <- prader_velocity_girls |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)


interpolated_prader_velocity |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_50, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_75, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_90, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_97, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_point(data = prader_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_3, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_10, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_25, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_50, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_75, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_90, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_97, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  scale_y_continuous(name = "velocity [cm]", expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Age [years]",
                     limits = c(0, 20), breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 20), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("LMS centiles" = "blue", "Empirical centiles" = "black"))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 0.5, l = 0.5, b = 0, unit = "cm"))



interpolated_prader_velocity |> 
  filter(sex == "f") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+

  geom_point(data = prader_velocity_girls, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_3, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of height velocity for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_prader_velocity_boys <- new_prader_velocity_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_velocity_girls <- new_prader_velocity_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_prader_height_velocity <- rbind(new_prader_velocity_boys, new_prader_velocity_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_prader_height_velocity, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_prader_height_velocity.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```




### Length length_velocity



The length_velocity for recumbent length is reported from 0.04 to 14.75 years and was normal distributed. Therefore, I will use L = 1 and S = SD/M.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add L values
# The L value is fixed to 1 because they reported a good accordance with a normal distribution

prader_length_velocity_boys <- prader_length_velocity_boys %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)

prader_length_velocity_girls <- prader_length_velocity_girls %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)

# Select M values

prader_length_velocity_boys <- prader_length_velocity_boys %>% 
  mutate(M = case_when(Age == 2.5 ~ NA,
                       TRUE ~ M))

prader_length_velocity_girls <- prader_length_velocity_girls %>% 
  mutate(M = case_when(Age == 2.5 ~ NA,
                       TRUE ~ M))

# calculate S values
prader_length_velocity_boys <- prader_length_velocity_boys %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_10/M)/(qnorm(0.10)),
                                           log(emp_perc_25/M)/(qnorm(0.25)),
                                           log(emp_perc_75/M)/(qnorm(0.75)),
                                           log(emp_perc_90/M)/(qnorm(0.90)),
                                           log(emp_perc_97/M)/(qnorm(0.97)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_length_velocity_boys <- prader_length_velocity_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)


prader_length_velocity_girls <- prader_length_velocity_girls %>%
  rowwise %>% 
  mutate(S_avg = case_when(L != 0 ~ mean(c(((emp_perc_3/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.03)),
                                           ((emp_perc_10/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.10)),
                                           ((emp_perc_25/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.25)),
                                           ((emp_perc_75/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.75)),
                                           ((emp_perc_90/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.90)),
                                           ((emp_perc_97/M)^L - 1)/(L*qnorm(0.97)))),
                           L == 0 ~ mean(c(log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)),
                                           log(emp_perc_3/M)/(qnorm(0.03)))))) %>% 
  ungroup()

prader_length_velocity_girls <- prader_length_velocity_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = S_avg)

# calculate age in days
prader_length_velocity_boys <- prader_length_velocity_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

prader_length_velocity_girls <- prader_length_velocity_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Age*365.25)

```

#### Check centiles

```{r}

new_prader_length_velocity_boys <- new_prader_length_velocity_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_length_velocity_girls <- new_prader_length_velocity_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")



interpolated_prader_length_velocity <- rbind(new_prader_length_velocity_boys, new_prader_length_velocity_girls)

interpolated_prader_length_velocity <- interpolated_prader_length_velocity |> 
  mutate(age_years = age_days/365.25)


z_score_centile_3 <- qnorm(0.03)
z_score_centile_10 <- qnorm(0.1)
z_score_centile_25 <- qnorm(0.25)
z_score_centile_50 <- qnorm(0.5)
z_score_centile_75 <- qnorm(0.75)
z_score_centile_90 <- qnorm(0.9)
z_score_centile_97 <- qnorm(0.97)

interpolated_prader_length_velocity <- interpolated_prader_length_velocity |> 
  mutate(centile_3 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_3)^(1 / L),
         centile_10 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_10)^(1 / L),
         centile_25 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_25)^(1 / L),
         centile_50 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_50)^(1 / L),
         centile_75 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_75)^(1 / L),
         centile_90 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_90)^(1 / L),
         centile_97 = M * (1 + L * S * z_score_centile_97)^(1 / L))


prader_length_velocity_boys <- prader_length_velocity_boys |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)

prader_length_velocity_girls <- prader_length_velocity_girls |> 
  mutate(age_years = Age)


interpolated_prader_length_velocity |> 
  filter(sex == "m") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age_years)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_3, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_10, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_25, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_50, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_75, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_90, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_97, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_3, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_10, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_25, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_50, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_75, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_90, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_boys, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_97, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  scale_y_continuous(name = "length_velocity [cm]", expand = c(0,0))+

  geom_line(aes(y = centile_90, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(y = centile_97, colour = "LMS centiles"), linewidth = 0.5)+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_girls, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_3, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_girls, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_10, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_girls, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_25, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_girls, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_50, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_girls, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_75, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_girls, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_90, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  geom_point(data = prader_length_velocity_girls, aes(x = age_years, y = emp_perc_97, colour = "Empirical centiles"))+
  scale_y_continuous(name = "length_velocity [cm]", expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Age [years]",
                     limits = c(0, 20), breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 20), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL,
                      values = c("LMS centiles" = "red", "Empirical centiles" = "black"))+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 0.5, l = 0.5, b = 0, unit = "cm"))

```


#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of height length_velocity for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_prader_length_velocity_boys <- new_prader_length_velocity_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_prader_length_velocity_girls <- new_prader_length_velocity_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_prader_length_velocity <- rbind(new_prader_length_velocity_boys, new_prader_length_velocity_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_prader_length_velocity, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_prader_length_velocity.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```



## Sempé references



### Length

The supine length references of Sempé were published from 0 to 216 months with mean and standard deviation values for every month.
Therefore, I will use L = 1 and S = SD/M.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add L values
# The L value is fixed to 1 because they reported a good accordance with a normal distribution

sempe_length_boys <- sempe_length_boys %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)

sempe_length_girls <- sempe_length_girls %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)


# create S values

sempe_length_boys <- sempe_length_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = SD/M)

sempe_length_girls <- sempe_length_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = SD/M)


# calculate age in days
sempe_length_boys <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

sempe_length_girls <- sempe_length_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

```


#### Boys

```{r}

# L parameter was fixed at 1.

# plot of published L-values

L_boys_plot <- ggplot(sempe_length_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=L))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("L (one)")+
  ggtitle("published LMS-values")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 3))

# Therefore, no interpolation necessary, always L=1

xout <- seq(0,ceiling(18*365.25), by=1)

new_L_boys <- data.frame(age_days = xout)
new_L_boys <- new_L_boys %>%
  mutate(L = 1)

# plot of interpolated L-values

L_boys_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_L_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=L))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("L (one)")+
  ggtitle("interpolated LMS-values")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 3))

# I need to interpolate the M parameter from the age 0 years to 18 years.

# plot of published M-values

M_boys_plot <- ggplot(sempe_length_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=M))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("M (cm)")

# I will use linear interpolation from month 0 to 1, cubic from 1 to 215, and linear from 215 to 216.

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(0,trunc(1/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(0*365.25)& age_days<=(1/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_M <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(0*365.25)& age_days<=(1/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(M) %>% 
  unlist()
new_M_1 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_M,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_M_1 <- rename(new_M_1, "age_days" = "x", "M" = "y")

# cubic interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(1/12*365.25),trunc(215/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(1/12*365.25)& age_days<=(215/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_M <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(1/12*365.25)& age_days<=(215/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(M) %>% 
  unlist()
new_M_2 <- data.frame(spline(x=x,y=y_M,xout=xout, method = "natural"))
new_M_2 <- rename(new_M_2, "age_days" = "x", "M" = "y")

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(215/12*365.25),ceiling(216/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(215/12*365.25) & age_days<=(216/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_M <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(215/12*365.25) & age_days<=(216/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(M) %>% 
  unlist()
new_M_3 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_M,xout=xout, method = "linear", rule = 2))
new_M_3 <- rename(new_M_3, "age_days" = "x", "M" = "y")

# merge all M-values

new_M_boys <- rbind(new_M_1, new_M_2, new_M_3)

# plot of interpolated M-values

M_boys_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_M_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=M))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("M (cm)")


# I need to interpolate the S parameter from the age 0 years to 18 years.

# plot of published S-values

S_boys_plot <- ggplot(sempe_length_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# I will use linear interpolation from month 0 to 1, cubic from 1 to 215, and linear from 215 to 216.

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(trunc(0*365.25),trunc(1/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(0*365.25)& age_days<=(1/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(0*365.25)& age_days<=(1/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_1 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_S_1 <- rename(new_S_1, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# cubic interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(1/12*365.25),trunc(215/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(1/12*365.25)& age_days<=(215/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(1/12*365.25)& age_days<=(215/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_2 <- data.frame(spline(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "natural"))
new_S_2 <- rename(new_S_2, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(ceiling(215/12*365.25),ceiling(216/12*365.25),by=1)
x <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(215/12*365.25) & age_days<=(216/12*365.25)) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- sempe_length_boys %>%
  filter(age_days>=(215/12*365.25) & age_days<=(216/12*365.25)) %>%
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_3 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear", rule = 2))
new_S_3 <- rename(new_S_3, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# merge all M-values

new_S_boys <- rbind(new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3)

# plot of interpolated S-values

S_boys_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_S_boys, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# merge all LMS-values

new_sempe_length_boys <- merge(x=new_L_boys, y=new_M_boys, by="age_days")
new_sempe_length_boys <- merge(x=new_sempe_length_boys, y=new_S_boys, by="age_days")

# create one figure with the 6 plots

interpolated_plot <- plot_grid(L_boys_plot, L_boys_interpolated_plot, M_boys_plot, M_boys_interpolated_plot, S_boys_plot, S_boys_interpolated_plot, labels = c(), ncol=2)

# print the figure

interpolated_plot

# delete temporary variables

rm(L_boys_plot, L_boys_interpolated_plot, M_boys_plot, M_boys_interpolated_plot, S_boys_plot, S_boys_interpolated_plot, interpolated_plot, new_L_boys, new_M_1, new_M_2, new_M_3, new_M_boys, new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3, new_S_boys)

```

### Height

The standing height references of Sempé were published from 30 to 252 months with mean and standard deviation values every 6 months.
Therefore, I will use L = 1 and S = SD/M.

```{r}
  mutate(L = 1)


# create S values

  mutate(S = SD/M)

  mutate(S = SD/M)

  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

sempe_height_girls <- sempe_height_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)
```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of height for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_sempe_height_boys <- new_sempe_height_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_sempe_height_girls <- new_sempe_height_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_sempe_height <- rbind(new_sempe_height_boys, new_sempe_height_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_sempe_height, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_sempe_height.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```



### Weight

The weight references of Sempé were published from 0 to 216 months with mean and standard deviation values for every month.
I did not read about the distribution of weights, but they always calculated an SD. I will still just use the heuristic L values from Hermanussen et al.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add L values

sempe_weight_boys <- sempe_weight_boys |> 
  mutate(Age = Month/12)

sempe_weight_boys <- left_join(sempe_weight_boys, hermanussen_weight_boys, by = "Age")


sempe_weight_girls <- sempe_weight_girls |> 
  mutate(Age = Month/12)

sempe_weight_girls <- left_join(sempe_weight_girls, hermanussen_weight_girls, by = "Age")


# create S values

sempe_weight_boys <- sempe_weight_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = SD/M)

sempe_weight_girls <- sempe_weight_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = SD/M)


# calculate age in days
sempe_weight_boys <- sempe_weight_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

sempe_weight_girls <- sempe_weight_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of weight for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_sempe_weight_boys <- new_sempe_weight_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_sempe_weight_girls <- new_sempe_weight_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_sempe_weight <- rbind(new_sempe_weight_boys, new_sempe_weight_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_sempe_weight, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_sempe_weight.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### Head circumference

The head circumference references of Sempé were published from 0 to 216 months with mean and standard deviation values for every month.
I did not read about the distribution of hcs, but they always calculated an SD. Therefore, I will use L = 1 and S = SD/M.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add L values
# The L value is fixed to 1 because they reported a good accordance with a normal distribution

sempe_hc_boys <- sempe_hc_boys %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)

sempe_hc_girls <- sempe_hc_girls %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)


# create S values

sempe_hc_boys <- sempe_hc_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = SD/M)

sempe_hc_girls <- sempe_hc_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = SD/M)


# calculate age in days
sempe_hc_boys <- sempe_hc_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

sempe_hc_girls <- sempe_hc_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

```

```{r}
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_sempe_hc <- rbind(new_sempe_hc_boys, new_sempe_hc_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_sempe_hc, here("data","processed", "Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_sempe_hc.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```



### Height velocity

The  height velocity references of Sempé were published from 12 to 240 months with mean and standard deviation values every 6 months. They did not report about distribution but calculated SDs. Therefore, I will use L = 1 and S = SD/M.


```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add L values
# The L value is fixed to 1 because they reported a good accordance with a normal distribution

sempe_velocity_boys <- sempe_velocity_boys %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)

sempe_velocity_girls <- sempe_velocity_girls %>% 
  mutate(L = 1)


# create S values

sempe_velocity_boys <- sempe_velocity_boys %>% 
  mutate(S = SD/M)

sempe_velocity_girls <- sempe_velocity_girls %>% 
  mutate(S = case_when(M == 0 ~ 0,
                       TRUE ~ SD/M))


# calculate age in days
sempe_velocity_boys <- sempe_velocity_boys %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

sempe_velocity_girls <- sempe_velocity_girls %>%
  mutate(age_days = Month/12*365.25)

```

## UK WHO references

The growth references used in the United Kingdom (UK) were published in 2009 [Cole et al.](https://doi.org/10.3109/03014460.2011.544139). They combined data from the WHO (MGRS) with data from the older 1990 UK growth references:

- Around birth, -3 weeks to 2 weeks: UK references 1990 (same LMS values for every day)
- 2 weeks to 4 years: WHO growth standards
- 4 years to 20 years: UK references 1990

### Length

I will use the UK reference 1990 from -3 weeks to 2 weeks, and the already available WHO growth standards from 2 weeks to 2 years.


```{r}

ukwho_height <- ukwho_height %>% 
  rename("sex" = "__SVJCKHsex", "age" = "__SVJCKHxvar", "L" = "__SVJCKHl", "M" = "__SVJCKHm", "S" = "__SVJCKHs") %>% 
  mutate(sex = case_when(sex == 1 ~ "m",
                         sex == 2 ~ "f"),
         age_days = age*365.25)

ukwho_length_boys <- ukwho_height %>% 
  filter(sex == "m") %>% 
  filter(age_days <= 730.5)

ukwho_length_girls <- ukwho_height %>% 
  filter(sex == "f") %>% 
  filter(age_days <= 730.5)

```

```{r}
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("L (one)")+
  ggtitle("interpolated LMS-values")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 3))

# I need to interpolate the M parameter from the age -3 weeks  to 2 years.

# plot of published M-values

M_girls_plot <- ggplot(ukwho_length_girls, aes(x=age_days, y=M))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("M (cm)")

# I will use linear interpolation from day -21 0 to 14, and the who growth standards from day 14 to 730.

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(-21,13,by=1)
x <- ukwho_length_girls %>%
  head(2) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_M <- ukwho_length_girls %>%
  head(2) %>% 
  select(M) %>% 
  unlist()
new_M_1 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_M,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_M_1 <- rename(new_M_1, "age_days" = "x", "M" = "y")

# who growth standards

new_M_2 <- who_length_girls %>% 
  filter(age_days>=14 & age_days <=730) %>% 
  select(age_days, M)

# merge all M-values

new_M_girls <- rbind(new_M_1, new_M_2)

# plot of interpolated M-values

M_girls_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_M_girls, aes(x=age_days, y=M))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("M (cm)")


# I need to interpolate the S parameter from the age -3 weeks  to 2 years.

# plot of published S-values

S_girls_plot <- ggplot(ukwho_length_girls, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# I will use linear interpolation from day -21 0 to 14, and the who growth standards from day 14 to 730.

# linear interpolation

xout <- seq(-21,13,by=1)
x <- ukwho_length_girls %>%
  head(2) %>% 
  select(age_days) %>% 
  unlist()
y_S <- ukwho_length_girls %>%
  head(2) %>% 
  select(S) %>% 
  unlist()
new_S_1 <- data.frame(approx(x=x,y=y_S,xout=xout, method = "linear",rule=2))
new_S_1 <- rename(new_S_1, "age_days" = "x", "S" = "y")

# who growth standards

new_S_2 <- who_length_girls %>% 
  filter(age_days>=14 & age_days <=730) %>% 
  select(age_days, S)

# merge all S-values

new_S_girls <- rbind(new_S_1, new_S_2)

# plot of interpolated S-values

S_girls_interpolated_plot <- ggplot(new_S_girls, aes(x=age_days, y=S))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab(" Age (days)")+
  ylab("S (one)")

# merge all LMS-values

new_ukwho_length_girls <- merge(x=new_L_girls, y=new_M_girls, by="age_days")
new_ukwho_length_girls <- merge(x=new_ukwho_length_girls, y=new_S_girls, by="age_days")

# create one figure with the 6 plots

interpolated_plot <- plot_grid(L_girls_plot, L_girls_interpolated_plot, M_girls_plot, M_girls_interpolated_plot, S_girls_plot, S_girls_interpolated_plot, labels = c(), ncol=2)

# print the figure

interpolated_plot

# delete temporary variables

rm(L_girls_plot, L_girls_interpolated_plot, M_girls_plot, M_girls_interpolated_plot, S_girls_plot, S_girls_interpolated_plot, interpolated_plot, new_L_girls, new_M_1, new_M_2, new_M_girls, new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_girls)

```


#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of length for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_ukwho_length_boys <- new_ukwho_length_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_ukwho_length_girls <- new_ukwho_length_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_ukwho_length <- rbind(new_ukwho_length_boys, new_ukwho_length_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_ukwho_length, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_ukwho_length.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```


### Height

I will use the already available WHO growth standards from year 2 to year 4, and interpolate the UK references 1990 from year 4 to year 20.


```{r}

ukwho_height_boys <- ukwho_height %>% 
  filter(sex == "m") %>% 
  filter(age_days >= 730.5)

ukwho_height_girls <- ukwho_height %>% 
  filter(sex == "f") %>% 
  filter(age_days >= 730.5)

```

### Weight

I will use the UK references from -21 days to 14 days, the WHO child growth references from 14 days to 4 years, and the UK references from 4 years to 20 years.

```{r}


ukwho_weight <- ukwho_weight %>% 
  rename("sex" = "__SVJCKHsex", "age" = "__SVJCKHxvar", "L" = "__SVJCKHl", "M" = "__SVJCKHm", "S" = "__SVJCKHs") %>% 
  mutate(sex = case_when(sex == 1 ~ "m",
                         sex == 2 ~ "f"),
         age_days = age*365.25)

ukwho_weight_boys <- ukwho_weight %>% 
  filter(sex == "m")

ukwho_weight_girls <- ukwho_weight %>% 
  filter(sex == "f")

```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of weight for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_ukwho_weight_boys <- new_ukwho_weight_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_ukwho_weight_girls <- new_ukwho_weight_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_ukwho_weight <- rbind(new_ukwho_weight_boys, new_ukwho_weight_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file
```

### BMI


I will use the WHO child growth references from 14 days to 4 years and the UK references from 4 years to 20 years.

```{r}


ukwho_bmi <- ukwho_bmi %>% 
  rename("sex" = "__SVJCKHsex", "age" = "__SVJCKHxvar", "L" = "__SVJCKHl", "M" = "__SVJCKHm", "S" = "__SVJCKHs") %>% 
  mutate(sex = case_when(sex == 1 ~ "m",
                         sex == 2 ~ "f"),
         age_days = age*365.25)

ukwho_bmi_boys <- ukwho_bmi %>% 
  filter(sex == "m")

ukwho_bmi_girls <- ukwho_bmi %>% 
  filter(sex == "f")

```

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_ukwho_bmi_boys <- new_ukwho_bmi_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_ukwho_bmi_girls <- new_ukwho_bmi_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_ukwho_bmi <- rbind(new_ukwho_bmi_boys, new_ukwho_bmi_girls)

write.csv(interpolated_ukwho_bmi, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_ukwho_bmi.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```

```{r}
  unlist()
```

```{r}
interpolated_plot

# delete temporary variables

rm(L_girls_plot, L_girls_interpolated_plot, M_girls_plot, M_girls_interpolated_plot, S_girls_plot, S_girls_interpolated_plot, interpolated_plot, new_L_1, new_L_2, new_L_3, new_L_4, new_L_5, new_L_girls, new_M_1, new_M_2, new_M_3, new_M_4, new_M_5, new_M_girls, new_S_1, new_S_2, new_S_3, new_S_4, new_S_5, new_S_girls)

```

#### Export interpolated LMS-values

I create a data frame with all the LMS-values of head circumference for boys and girls and export the data frame as a csv file.

```{r}
#| output: true
#| warning: false

# add sex variable to LMS-values

new_ukwho_hc_boys <- new_ukwho_hc_boys %>%
  mutate(sex="m")

new_ukwho_hc_girls <- new_ukwho_hc_girls %>%
  mutate(sex="f")

# create a data frame with the LMS-values for boys and girls

interpolated_ukwho_hc <- rbind(new_ukwho_hc_boys, new_ukwho_hc_girls)

# export the data frame as a csv file

write.csv(interpolated_ukwho_hc, here("data","processed","Interpolated-growth-references","interpolated_ukwho_hc.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```
